name: P_equals_NP

phase_0.boundary_condition: The polynomial hierarchy boundary closes the system; it is the terminal anchor that contains all complexity classes and their relativized extensions, beyond which no computational question can be formulated without collapsing the hierarchy itself.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized complexity landscape before P=NP is postulated; no classes, reductions, or witnesses exist yet.

⊣.justification: The closed containment that bounds all complexity classes; the hierarchy cannot be exited without collapsing it entirely.

≻.justification: The forward morphism where polynomial-time verification catalyzes polynomial-time generation; the certificate becomes the solution.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism retracing a solution back to its certificate; the computational arrow of time folded onto itself.

⋈.justification: Sequential composition of Karp-Levin reductions linking NP-complete problems; each link preserves polynomial-time equivalence.

⊙.justification: The μ∘δ=id fixed point at the horn torus pinch; the equivalence recognizes itself as the critical threshold.

∈.justification: The search space splits into two arms: the verification arm (polynomial-time certificate checking) and the generation arm (exponential candidate enumeration).

∋.justification: The arms rejoin at the critical point where a single polynomial-time algorithm synthesizes the witness for all instances simultaneously.

⊤.justification: Constructive truth: a polynomial-time verifier accepts the certificate, establishing the affirmative arm.

⊥.justification: Constructive falsity: the exponential enumeration finds no certificate, establishing the negative arm.

⊞.justification: At the phase transition, P=NP and P≠NP are held simultaneously as a live contradiction (B-state); the paradigm does not resolve, it persists.

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation of the complexity class equality; once recorded, the polynomial hierarchy cannot be restored to separation.

phase_3.void_description: No complexity classes defined; no decision problems, no reductions, no witnesses. The empty state before Cook-Levin.
phase_3.true_description: Polynomial-time verification succeeds; a certificate is accepted in deterministic polynomial time. The affirmative arm of the bifurcation.
phase_3.false_description: Exponential enumeration completes without finding a certificate; the search space is exhausted. The negative arm of the bifurcation.
phase_3.both_description: The critical phase where verification and generation coincide: a polynomial-time algorithm exists that both checks and produces certificates. The B-state is the equivalence itself — neither true nor false alone, but both simultaneously held at the phase transition.
